plan.title: Colon RSEM counts: treated vs control DE + GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single gene-level RSEM matrix (/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv, 12,000 genes x 12 samples, gene symbols in column 1) with a 12-row metadata table carrying one condition column: 6 treated vs 6 control human colon samples, unpaired, single batch. The research question is a plain two-group differential expression contrast, so the plan is one linear DE track (T1) with an enrichment branch (T2) and a consolidated report.

Two data facts drive the method choices. First, the counts are RSEM expected counts, which are not integers. The canonical route (tximport type='rsem', carrying per-gene effective lengths into the model as an offset) is NOT available here because the per-sample genes.results files were not delivered — only the summarized matrix was. The plan therefore states explicitly that T1S2 must round the expected counts to integers for DESeqDataSetFromMatrix and record in the report that the effective-length offset could not be applied, with the consequence that a gene whose effective length shifts between conditions is not corrected. This is a stated deviation, not a silent one.

Second, sample_01 has a library size roughly 4x below the median. It is kept through QC, plotted on the PCA and the sample-distance heatmap, and its library size and detected-gene count are reported beside the others. Median-of-ratios size factors already account for depth and a low-depth sample simply carries wider confidence intervals; it is removed only if the QC step finds an independent reason (failed library, group-discordant clustering) and states it. A sensitivity re-run without it is included as an explicit contingency in T1S2 rather than a default.

Inference is DESeq2 Wald on ~condition with control set as the explicit reference so a positive log2FC means higher in treated, apeglm shrinkage for ranking and plots, BH at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering on, and the p-value histogram inspected before the adjustment is trusted. With 6 per group, DESeq2 flags Cook's-distance count outliers to NA rather than replacing them; those NAs are reported separately from independent-filter NAs. edgeR quasi-likelihood runs on the same filtered matrix as a second method and the intersection is the high-confidence set. Enrichment is fgsea preranked on the full tested list ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the disputed-metric choice, stated here), against human MSigDB Hallmark first and then human Reactome; an over-representation test is deliberately not the primary method, and is only permissible if well over 50 genes pass FDR.

steps.method: Sample structure QC: blind VST, PCA on top 500 variable genes, sample distance heatmap, library sizes
Keep genes with at least 10 counts in at least 6 samples (smallest group size)
~ condition with control as explicit reference level; RSEM expected counts rounded because per-sample genes.results with effective lengths were not delivered
DESeq2 Wald test, plus edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test as a second method for overlap
Benjamini-Hochberg with independent filtering, alpha 0.05, p-value histogram inspected
fgsea preranked GSEA on the DESeq2 Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark, then Reactome
Consolidated report with MA plot, dispersion plot, effect columns, leading edge genes, session info

acceptance_criteria: Reports the method, package versions, the design formula ~condition, the contrast (condition, treated, control), the alpha and any fold-change threshold, the number of genes tested after filtering, and the number of DE genes
Carries an MA plot and a dispersion plot, placed before the gene tables, each with a one-line statement of what it shows
Gene table gives unshrunken log2FoldChange, apeglm-shrunken log2FoldChange, and lfcSE per gene, with genes ranked by the shrunken value and the shrinkage estimator named in the header

Reports DESeq2 and edgeR significant counts and the intersection, presenting the intersection as the high-confidence set and any method-specific genes as a labelled secondary set — never the union as the headline
Lists leading-edge genes per significant gene set with each member's gene-level statistic, and marks leading-edge overlap between reported sets
States the gene set database, its version, the rank metric (DESeq2 Wald statistic), the universe, and the 15-500 size window
States explicitly that RSEM effective-length offsets were unavailable and expected counts were rounded, and what that does not correct for
States sample_01's library size relative to the median, the keep/drop decision, its reason, and — if a sensitivity re-run was done — how the DE counts compared
Includes a reproducibility record: sessionInfo, package versions, the random seed, and the pinned gene set collection version
constraints: Rank genes and draw plots on the shrunken log2 fold change; keep p-values from the unshrunken fit
State that enrichment results are method-dependent and present enriched sets as hypotheses for follow-up
Do not present the union of DESeq2 and edgeR calls as the primary result
If the DE list is short or empty, say so plainly and do not loosen the threshold to manufacture a result
Do not overstate a mechanism from pathway names alone
caveats: 6 vs 6 unpaired with no batch information is a clean but modestly powered design; effect sizes from 12,000 tested genes at this n are imprecise
No external validation cohort is part of this analysis, so every finding here is internal to these 12 colon samples

grounding.reason: Report content follows the returned report-step rules: method/versions/design/thresholds (R-0041@059a), MA and dispersion diagnostics (R-0087@c53d), shrunken and unshrunken effects with ranking on the shrunken value (R-0085@c24d), DESeq2/edgeR intersection as the high-confidence set (R-0042@54e1), leading-edge listing (R-0105@c4a8), and a full reproducibility record (R-0086@becf).
